title: I ran out of Fable 5 tokens — anyone want to continue developing this roguelike shooter?
author: uskyeeeee
selftext:
I made a top-down roguelike shooter where everything is built entirely with code. There are no art assets required.  
The interesting part is that if you use Fable 5, you can basically tell it something like:  
“Add 5 new enemies, 10 new guns, and 1 boss.”  
And honestly, I believe it can do a pretty good job.  
The development journey itself was also interesting. I originally built this game with Gemini and OPUS, and at that stage I finished most of the game’s modules except for the dungeon system. But development was still pretty difficult back then. I would often run into issues that required many repeated attempts before the AI could finally solve them.  
After Fable 5 appeared, everything suddenly became much simpler. I only needed to tell it what I wanted, and it could immediately implement it. The entire development experience changed qualitatively.  
Unfortunately, I’ve already used up all of my Fable 5 tokens for this week, but I really want to see this game keep evolving.  
What I’m hoping for is not that people fork it and build separate versions, but that people contribute directly to the same codebase through PRs. I want to see whether, in an era where development is becoming this simple, a group of people can iterate on the same game together — adding enemies, weapons, bosses, mechanics, balance changes, and polish — until it becomes something far beyond what one person originally started.  
I also hope more people can experience the joy of making games on the web. That joy might be even greater than the joy of playing games themselves. It is a kind of creative happiness that simply didn’t exist in the previous era.  
Here’s the GitHub repo:  
[https://github.com/ssochi/rouge](https://github.com/ssochi/rouge)  
PRs are very welcome. Please contribute back to this repo instead of building separate forks — I’d love to see what we can create together in one shared codebase.

comments.author: robogame_dev
comments.body: You realize anything you can do in 3 prompts in fable you can do in 4-5 prompts in any other LLM right? Just write slightly smaller prompts - you can do it.

replies.author: uskyeeeee
replies.body:
From my experience, once the task becomes more complex, other models require you to break the task down and repeatedly review/validate the results. With Fable, I don’t really have to do that.  
So yes, maybe Fable can do it in one or two prompts, and other models can do it in four or five, but the amount of human effort involved is completely different. And I’m making this project just for fun. The experience and the positive feedback loop I get from Fable are far better than with other models.

replies.author: loontoon
replies.body:
I've used Fable a lot and don't see how you think it can build a game in one or two prompts.  

I've probably written 500 prompts across all the models I'm using, maybe more seeing as I have about 400 commits on my project; and my game is probably 4-6 months away from any kind of launch readiness. 

I do of course appreciate that "a game" means a lot of different things, but maybe people should be a little more expansive with their definitions and comments.

replies.author: uskyeeeee
replies.body:
When did I ever say that one or two prompts can build an entire game?  
What I meant was that for a specific complex task or feature, Fable often needs much less breakdown and manual validation than other models. That’s very different from saying a whole game can be made in one or two prompts.  
And if that were really what I believed, why would I even make this post? The whole point is that the project still needs many iterations, and I’m hoping more people can join in and contribute.

replies.author: loontoon
replies.body:
Maybe you didn't mean it could build a complete game, but there are lots of people who are - I was at a coding meetup here in Bangkok yesterday and guy was talking about some youtube video about Fable one shotting games. 

When I saw your comment in my notifications I admit I didn't check what thread it was and thought you were refering to Fable building a game in a few prompts.

Second, the point wasn’t to insult you. The point is that vibe coders don’t need other vibe coders’ services. There’s literally no value in that. It’s like trying to sell someone air or dust.
